messages:
marta: noticing a noticeable LCP bump on /dashboard EU canary after the telemetry-proxy rollout. heatmap and sparklines slower in traces, looks like main-thread parse spikes. replay: https://replay.internal/abc123 :thinking:
kevin: same. flamegraph shows big parse time from a new chunk + a bunch of KV cache misses. bundle for metrics pane grew ~70-120KB depending on gzip
sam: I repro locally. new dependency `viz-serializer` is executed during nav; it's imported at top of metrics pane and runs sync during hover/render prep. that explains parse spike
olivia: I added the serializer to speed up CSV export, kept it synchronous to avoid stream complexity. didn't expect it to be eagerly parsed on nav prefetch
marta: telemetry also shows a kvcache miss storm at the same timestamps. we added a metric-id namespace last week; maybe lookups changed and prefixes miss causing rehydration of big payloads
kevin: two separate but related issues: prefetch policy is too aggressive (we prefetch top-level chunks on nav), and prefetches are being counted against route quotas which triggers infra throttles. fetches get delayed -> parse windows collide with UI work
sam: short term fix: make serializer lazy-loaded and guard prefetch with device/check and chart count. pseudo:
```javascript
if (chartsVisible > 1 && !isLowEndDevice()) {
  prefetch('/chunks/viz-serializer.js', { purpose: 'prefetch' })
}
```
This keeps desktop fast while avoiding wasted parse on mobile/low-end
kevin: also set a header (X-Purpose: prefetch) so infra can exclude these from quota accounting. right now prefetches look like regular route traffic and trip quota-based backpressure
olivia: I'll swap to dynamic import() and create a slim CSV-only serializer chunk. will add explicit chunkName so bundler keeps it split: `import(/* webpackChunkName: "viz-serializer" */ './serializer')`
marta: can we rollback the telemetry-proxy canary while we stabilize? routing + kvcache mismatch seems coupled. @deploy-bot can you rollback the canary-proxy to previous sha?
deploy-bot: rollback request acknowledged from marta 1 initiating rollback of canary-proxy -> sha abc123. est completion ~2m :hourglass_flowing_sand:
sam: opening PR with conditional prefetch, purpose header, and telemetry hooks for `prefetch.requested` / `prefetch.blocked`. also adding kvcache.lookup.variant to events so we can see schema mismatches
kevin: please ensure telemetry exposes prefetch latency buckets and quota-related response metadata. I'll follow up with infra to consider ignoring prefetch X-Purpose in quota math for client-side prefetches
olivia: PR up: https://github.com/redwood/viz/pull/444 0 includes dynamic import, explicit chunk name, prefetch gating, and a smaller csv-streamer build. left a fallback for really old browsers
marta: after initiating rollback I can see median LCP on EU canary samples drop ~350-420ms. looks promising. let's run a 10% EU canary with Olivia's changes and gate telemetry for 48h before full re-promote :party:
kevin: agree. add an alert if median LCP > baseline +200ms and an increased kvcache miss rate alert. also request infra to prototype excluding prefetch requests from route quota accounting
nsam: noted. I'll add the alert and the canary manifest change in the PR description
olivia: I'll also put a CI measurement for parse time of the trimmed serializer so we catch regressions pre-merge
marta: follow-ups/tickets: 1) telemetry key migration doc for metric-id namespace (sam), 2) infra change to exclude prefetch X-Purpose from quota calc (kevin), 3) release small csv-serializer and add parse-time CI (olivia). i'll file them after closing this thread
kevin: quick PR nit: prefer `X-Purpose: prefetch` over custom query param. otherwise LGTM once telemetry events are wired
sam: thanks all. will monitor and post canary results in #eng-platform in 24h
deploy-bot: rollback complete for canary-proxy -> sha abc123. monitoring metrics for the next 30m
